    pub(crate) fn register_binding(&mut self, range: TextRange, text: TokenText) {
        self.js_bindings.insert(range, text);
    }

        embed_block_kind: Option<&EmbedBlockKind>,

        for event in preorder {

Done. The fix is in `crates/biome_service/src/workspace/document/services/embedded_bindings.rs`.

## What was wrong

When Biome collects the variables declared by a Svelte snippet, a parameter with a default value (`figure(image = fallback)`) parses as a JS **assignment expression**. The existing `visit_svelte_call_bindings` handled the assignment-expression case by only registering the LHS *if it was a plain identifier* (`left.as_any_js_assignment()?.as_js_identifier_assignment()?`). Any destructuring LHS (`{ src } = fallback`, `[a, b] = fallback`, etc.) fell through and registered nothing — so those parameter variables were treated as undeclared and produced false-positive `lint/correctness/noUndeclaredVariables` diagnostics.

## The change

I replaced the identifier-only branch with a recursive walk of the full assignment-pattern LHS, adding two helpers:

- **`visit_svelte_assignment_pattern`** — handles the three `AnyJsAssignmentPattern` shapes: plain identifier, object destructuring, and array destructuring (including array rest elements), recursing for nesting.
- **`visit_svelte_object_assignment_member`** — registers each object member: keyed properties (recurses into the value pattern), shorthand properties, and `...rest` targets.

This registers the bound variables for all required cases while the right-hand default value stays a *reference* (never registered as a binding), so:
- `image = fallback` → `image`
- `{ src, caption } = fallback` → `src`, `caption`
- `[first, second] = emptyList` → `first`, `second`
- `{ item: { src } = fallback }` → `src`
- `[{ id } = fallback]` → `id`
- `{ src, ...rest } = fallback` → `src`, `rest`

Variables used in a snippet body that aren't bound by a parameter and aren't declared in an outer scope still aren't registered, so they continue to be flagged; and outer-scope variables used as defaults are no longer false-positived.

All 18 existing `embedded_bindings` tests pass, and I confirmed the six new cases behave correctly with a temporary test (since removed). No files under `tests/` were touched.
